issues.title: Command not found
issues.symptom: The shell cannot locate the requested executable.
issues.cause: Install missing, old PATH, or wrong environment.
issues.check: Use `command -v TOOL` in Bash, `Get-Command TOOL` in PowerShell, or `where TOOL` in CMD, replacing TOOL.
issues.fix: Install from the tool page, reopen the shell, and check that the installer’s executable directory is on your user PATH.
issues.verify: Run the tool’s documented `--version` command in the same shell.

issues.title: npm EACCES / permission denied
issues.symptom: A global npm install cannot write its target directory.
issues.cause: Node or the npm prefix belongs to another user.
issues.check: Check `npm config get prefix` and whether Node came from a system package or a user-owned installation.
issues.fix: Use a supported user-owned Node installation. Do not run `sudo npm` or recursively change system ownership.
issues.verify: Reopen the shell, check Node/npm versions, then retry the official package install.

issues.title: Externally managed Python
issues.symptom: pip refuses to modify the system Python.
issues.cause: The OS manages that Python environment.
issues.check: Check `python3 --version` and which interpreter the command uses.
issues.fix: Create `python3 -m venv .venv` and use its Python explicitly. Install the distro’s venv package if missing.
issues.verify: Run `.venv/bin/python -m pip --version`; Windows uses `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip --version`.

issues.title: Package build failed
issues.symptom: A dependency fails while compiling or has no matching wheel/binary.
issues.cause: Unsupported Python/Node major, architecture, libc, or missing compiler.
issues.check: Record OS, architecture, runtime versions, and the first meaningful compiler error; redact paths or values as needed.
issues.fix: Use the tool’s supported runtime. Install documented build prerequisites, or move to a supported host when no Android binary exists.
issues.verify: Install cleanly and run the package’s documented version check and a small task.

issues.title: Unsupported Node engine
issues.symptom: npm reports that the selected package requires another Node version.
issues.cause: The installed runtime is outside the package’s supported range.
issues.check: Run `node --version` and read the package’s engines/installation requirements.
issues.fix: Install a supported current LTS from an official source. Do not treat `--force` as compatibility.
issues.verify: Run `node --version`, reinstall with the intended runtime, and launch the tool.

issues.title: pnpm / Corepack not found
issues.symptom: A tutorial assumes a command your Node installation did not provide.
issues.cause: Corepack bundling and package-manager installation differ by release.
issues.check: Run `node --version`, `npm --version`, and `command -v pnpm` in Bash.
issues.fix: Follow pnpm’s current official installation method; do not assume Corepack is bundled.
issues.verify: Run `pnpm --version` and the project’s lockfile-preserving install command.

issues.title: PowerShell blocks npm.ps1
issues.symptom: PowerShell refuses to execute the npm wrapper script.
issues.cause: Execution policy blocks the `.ps1` shim.
issues.check: Check whether `npm.cmd --version` works in the same terminal.
issues.fix: Use `npm.cmd` or the official tool’s native binary. Avoid changing machine-wide execution policy for this issue.
issues.verify: Run the intended npm command using `npm.cmd` and verify the installed tool.

issues.title: A similarly named program launches
issues.symptom: The executable has unexpected help text or behavior.
issues.cause: An unrelated package or earlier PATH entry shadows the intended tool.
issues.check: Inspect its version and command location; compare the package publisher and repository with the tool page.
issues.fix: Remove only the identified incorrect package using its package manager, then install the official package.
issues.verify: Check the publisher, executable path, and version before authenticating.

issues.title: 401 / invalid API key
issues.symptom: Provider rejects authentication.
issues.cause: Wrong provider key, expired/revoked key, missing environment, or wrong auth route.
issues.check: Check only whether the expected variable is configured using the doctor; review the endpoint and selected provider.
issues.fix: Load a valid key through a hidden prompt or documented auth flow. Remove accidental whitespace. Never print the value for debugging.
issues.verify: Run one small authorized request and check account usage.

issues.title: 403 / access denied
issues.symptom: Authentication may succeed but access is refused.
issues.cause: Model, organization, region, policy, or account entitlement does not allow this request.
issues.check: Read the redacted provider error and confirm the official account/project/model requirements.
issues.fix: Choose a route your account legitimately supports or contact provider support. Do not bypass policy or region restrictions.
issues.verify: Retry only after the entitlement/configuration issue is resolved.

issues.title: 429 / too many requests
issues.symptom: Provider rejects requests for rate or quota reasons.
issues.cause: Per-minute limit, exhausted allowance, or upstream capacity.
issues.check: Inspect retry guidance, account usage, selected free variant, and concurrent agent sessions.
issues.fix: Wait as instructed, reduce concurrency/context where relevant, or deliberately choose an available authorized route. Do not rotate accounts to evade limits.
issues.verify: One small request succeeds without a retry storm; usage stays within the intended budget.

issues.title: Unexpected model charges
issues.symptom: A task consumes paid usage despite a free-software label.
issues.cause: CLI license was confused with model pricing, fallback selected a paid route, or retries expanded usage.
issues.check: Stop the agent and inspect account usage, exact model ID, routing/fallback, and API-vs-subscription billing.
issues.fix: Set supported budget controls, select the intended route, and revoke an exposed key if usage is unauthorized.
issues.verify: Run a small deliberate task and compare usage to expected pricing.

issues.title: Old Gemini consumer login stopped working
issues.symptom: A formerly working personal Gemini CLI sign-in no longer grants requests.
issues.cause: Google announced a consumer transition to Antigravity CLI in June 2026.
issues.check: Check authentication type, tool version, and the official transition notice linked in the Gemini guide.
issues.fix: Follow the documented migration or an eligible API/enterprise route. Do not assume old free-quota screenshots apply.
issues.verify: Confirm the selected product/account route and its current allowance in a new small session.

issues.title: Configured key is not visible to the CLI
issues.symptom: A key exists in one shell or file but the program cannot see it.
issues.cause: Different process, OS userland, GUI launch environment, or a client that does not load `.env`.
issues.check: Check the client’s loading rules and presence-only doctor in the same launch environment.
issues.fix: Load the variable into that process using the documented mechanism; restart the client when required.
issues.verify: Check configured/not-configured status without displaying the key, then authenticate.

issues.title: Key appeared in Git or a screenshot
issues.symptom: A real credential was published or shared.
issues.cause: Secret was included in tracked content, logs, command history, or an image.
issues.check: Identify the affected provider and key using non-secret metadata; do not repost the secret.
issues.fix: Revoke/rotate immediately, review usage, replace legitimate secret stores, and follow the API-key incident guide.
issues.verify: The old credential is invalid; new secrets are scoped and absent from tracked files/history remediation targets.

issues.title: Model not found
issues.symptom: The provider cannot resolve the requested model.
issues.cause: Wrong ID/tag, missing local download, wrong provider prefix, or model removal.
issues.check: Use `ollama list` locally or inspect the provider’s current model catalog; compare exact identifiers.
issues.fix: Pull the intended local tag or select an available remote ID. Aider provider prefixes are part of its syntax.
issues.verify: A small inference request succeeds with the displayed intended model.

issues.title: Connection refused on 11434
issues.symptom: Client cannot reach the Ollama server.
issues.cause: Server stopped, wrong machine/port, broken SSH tunnel, or incorrect base URL.
issues.check: Check the host running the server and `ollama list`; inspect the documented service status or manual server terminal.
issues.fix: Start the official service or one manual `ollama serve` instance; correct the endpoint/tunnel. Do not expose a public unauthenticated port.
issues.verify: `ollama list` and a tiny local request work from the intended client.

issues.title: Address already in use
issues.symptom: A service cannot bind its requested port.
issues.cause: Another process already owns the port, often the existing Ollama app.
issues.check: Inspect running applications and the current server; on supported Linux use `ss -ltn` for listening TCP ports.
issues.fix: Use the existing intended server or stop only the identified conflicting process. Choose a different preview port if appropriate.
issues.verify: Exactly one intended service answers on the chosen port.

issues.title: Out of memory / process killed
issues.symptom: Inference or build fails during loading or long context.
issues.cause: Weights, KV cache, concurrency, OS, and other apps exceed memory.
issues.check: Check available RAM/VRAM, loaded models via `ollama ps`, context settings, and other applications.
issues.fix: Use a smaller/stronger quantization where appropriate, shorter context, and one request; move heavy work to suitable hardware.
issues.verify: Complete a representative small task without swapping excessively or being killed.

issues.title: CUDA / GPU unavailable
issues.symptom: Model runs on CPU or the GPU backend fails.
issues.cause: Unsupported hardware, mismatched driver/runtime, unavailable device passthrough, or insufficient VRAM.
issues.check: Compare exact hardware/driver/OS with Ollama’s current GPU documentation; inspect `ollama ps` processor allocation.
issues.fix: Follow vendor-supported driver guidance. WSL and containers need their own device support; Android PRoot is not desktop CUDA.
issues.verify: A known small model reports the intended processor allocation; otherwise use an honest CPU route.

issues.title: Malformed tool calls or broken edits
issues.symptom: Chat works but the agent cannot perform reliable actions.
issues.cause: Model lacks required tool/edit format, context is too small, or protocol compatibility is partial.
issues.check: Check agent/provider/model tool support and inspect a minimal non-sensitive task.
issues.fix: Use a documented tool-capable model or a client with a suitable text-editing mode. Keep permissions intact.
issues.verify: The small task completes with valid actions and independently passing tests.

issues.title: Context window exceeded
issues.symptom: Request exceeds token or local memory limits.
issues.cause: Too many files, long history, verbose tool output, or reserved output budget.
issues.check: Inspect selected files and the exact model/runtime context settings.
issues.fix: Start a focused session, select fewer files, summarize relevant history, and keep output budget. Increasing context also costs memory/tokens.
issues.verify: A focused task completes without truncating essential requirements.

issues.title: Termux storage permission / symlink failure
issues.symptom: Packages or executables fail under shared phone storage.
issues.cause: Shared storage is not a normal executable Unix filesystem.
issues.check: Run `pwd` and check whether the repository is under `/sdcard` or a storage shortcut.
issues.fix: Clone into `~/projects`; use `termux-setup-storage` only when exporting/importing user files.
issues.verify: Install dependencies and run a small script from Termux internal storage.

issues.title: Illegal instruction / unsupported architecture
issues.symptom: A native program crashes or cannot execute.
issues.cause: Binary targets the wrong CPU, libc, OS ABI, or unsupported instruction set.
issues.check: Record `uname -m`, runtime version, native Termux versus PRoot, and the first error.
issues.fix: Use a matching upstream-supported build; choose SSH/browser development if none exists. Do not rename binaries or trust random patched packages.
issues.verify: Version check and a small task run in the intended environment.

issues.title: Browser says localhost refused connection
issues.symptom: Browser cannot reach the development server.
issues.cause: Server stopped, wrong port, phone background suspension, or server is actually remote.
issues.check: Check the running terminal, printed port, and which machine hosts the server.
issues.fix: Restart the server; use local loopback on-device, authenticated cloud preview, or an SSH tunnel for a remote host.
issues.verify: Open the correct URL while the server/tunnel remains running.

issues.title: WSL tools or file watchers behave strangely
issues.symptom: Windows and Linux packages/files conflict or builds are slow.
issues.cause: Mixed PATH/runtime or project dependencies shared across filesystems.
issues.check: Run `pwd`, `command -v node`, and check WSL version from PowerShell.
issues.fix: Keep Linux clones in `~/projects`, install Linux dependencies in WSL, and use supported WSL 2 where needed.
issues.verify: The correct Linux executable runs and the project builds in its own environment.

issues.title: macOS blocks application or folder access
issues.symptom: Gatekeeper or privacy controls prevent launch/file access.
issues.cause: Unverified publisher or missing narrowly scoped file permission.
issues.check: Check the official installer source and exact macOS dialog.
issues.fix: Follow vendor/Apple instructions for the specific app and folder. Do not disable Gatekeeper globally or grant Full Disk Access by default.
issues.verify: The verified app opens the intended project without unnecessary permissions.

issues.title: Cloud Shell loses installed packages
issues.symptom: A new session lacks a previous system installation.
issues.cause: The VM environment is ephemeral while supported home storage is persistent.
issues.check: Check `pwd`, tool version, and whether files lived in the persistent home area.
issues.fix: Keep source in Git, use documented user-level installs, and record reproducible setup instructions.
issues.verify: A fresh session can restore tooling and the pushed repository.

issues.title: Git reports merge conflicts
issues.symptom: Local and incoming edits overlap.
issues.cause: Branches changed the same part of a file.
issues.check: Run `git status` and inspect both sides of each conflict.
issues.fix: Resolve the intended content, stage specific files, run tests, and complete the merge. Avoid force push as a generic repair.
issues.verify: No conflict markers remain; tests pass; the staged diff contains the intended combined behavior.
